'''Roland Post Falkner''' (April 14, 1866 – November 27, 1940) was an American [[economist]] and [[statistician]].<ref name=dab>{{Cite DAB|title=Falkner, Roland Post|volume=Supplement Two|year=1958|author=Paul J. FitzPatrick}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Robert P. Falkner was born in [[Bridgeport, Connecticut]] on April 14, 1866.<ref name=Twentieth>{{Cite book |url=https://archive.org/details/biographicaldict04johnuoft/page/n52/mode/1up |title=The Twentieth Century Biographical Dictionary of Notable Americans |volume=IV |editor1-first=Rossiter |editor1-last=Johnson |editor2-first=John Howard |editor2-last=Brown |publisher=American Biographical Society |location=Boston |page=<!-- no page numbers --> |year=1906 |access-date=2022-03-18 |via=Internet Archive}}</ref>

He graduated from the [[University of Pennsylvania]] (Wharton School of Finance and Economy) in 1885; studied economics at [[Humboldt University of Berlin|Berlin]], [[University of Leipzig|Leipzig]] and [[University of Halle|Halle-on-Saale]], Germany; studied at the [[Collège de France]]; was instructor in accounting and statistics in the University of Pennsylvania in 1888–91, and professor of statistics 1891–1900.<ref name=dab /><ref name=ea>{{Cite Americana|wstitle=Falkner, Roland Post|short=x|vb=1}}</ref>

He served also as statistician of the [[United States Senate]] Committee of Finance in 1891; as secretary of the United States delegation to the [[Brussels Monetary Conference (1892)|International Monetary Conference]] in [[Brussels]]; and as secretary of that conference in 1892.<ref name=ea /> He left the University of Pennsylvania in 1900 for the [[Library of Congress]], where he was chief of the division of documents.<ref name=dab /> From 1904 to 1907 he served as commissioner of education in [[Puerto Rico]]; from 1908 to 1911 he was statistician in charge of school inquiries for the [[United States Immigration Commission]], and in 1911-12 was assistant director of the [[United States Census|census]].<ref name=ea /> From 1915 until 1926 he was associated with the [[Alexander Hamilton Institute]], and from 1926 onward with the [[National Industrial Conference Board]].<ref name=dab />

In 1894 he was elected to the International Institute of Statistics.<ref name=dab /> In 1920 he was elected as a [[Fellow]] of the [[American Statistical Association]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=WcXxAAAAMAAJ&pg=PA647 |title=Quarterly Publications of the American Statistical Association |publisher=[[American Statistical Association]] |volume=17 |page=647 |year=1920 |access-date=2022-03-18 |via=Google Books}}</ref>

He died at [[Memorial Hospital (New York City, New York)|Memorial Hospital]] in New York on November 27, 1940.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/97875844/dr-roland-p-falkner-noted-economist/ |title=Dr. Roland P. Falkner, Noted Economist, Dies |newspaper=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]] |location=New York |agency=AP |page=5 |date=1940-11-29 |access-date=2022-03-18 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref>

== Works ==
{{wikisource|works=or}}
He is author of numerous essays on criminology, sociology, etc. to economic, statistical and other journals; and was editor of ''Annals'' of the [[American Academy of Political and Social Science]] 1890–1900.<ref name=ea /> He did a notable study of prices and wages in the United States for the [[United States Senate]]. It was published as "Retail Prices and Wages" (1892) and "Wholesale Prices, Wages, and Transportation" (1893).<ref name=dab /><ref>{{cite book|author=Roland P. Falkner|title=Wholesale Prices: 1890 to 1899 ...|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=qF7GAAAAMAAJ|year=1900|publisher=U.S. Government Printing Office|oclc=17634442}}</ref> He published a translation of [[August Meitzen]]'s ''History, Theory, and Technique of Statistics'' (1893).<ref name=ea /><ref>{{cite book|author=August Meitzen|title=History, Theory, and Technique of Statistics|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=C48YAAAAMAAJ|volume=Part One|year=1891|publisher=[[American Academy of Political and Social Science]]}}</ref>
